requirements.source_phrase: A shop owner signs up with an email and password and lands in their own new workspace
requirements.statement: A visitor can sign up with an email and password from /signup and lands in a new, empty workspace of their own whose name reads exactly as entered
requirements.notes: Entry point for every other flow; the workspace name is the value the user typed, not a generated default.

requirements.source_phrase: A shop owner signs up with an email and password and lands in their own new workspace
requirements.statement: POST /api/auth/signup stores the user and creates exactly one workspace owned by that user; a second signup with the same email is refused and stores no second user
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of signup: uniqueness of the email is enforced by the store, not only by the form.

requirements.source_phrase: a member signs in with their email and password and sees their workspace
requirements.statement: Signing in at /signin with a seeded account's credentials lands on the dashboard listing that account's own products and nothing from another workspace

requirements.source_phrase: a member signs in with their email and password and sees their workspace
requirements.statement: POST /api/auth/signin returns a session for correct credentials and refuses a wrong password with no session and no token in the response

requirements.source_phrase: The testing system depends on these two accounts and these exact passwords
requirements.statement: The two seeded accounts owner@shop.test / Owner123! and staff@shop.test / Staff123! both sign in, and each belongs to exactly one workspace named in the seed (the owner's workspace and the second workspace respectively)
requirements.notes: Every later phase seeds from these values; the cross-tenant checks depend on the two accounts living in different workspaces.

requirements.source_phrase: Users can add a product with a name, SKU, unit cost, quantity and low-stock threshold
requirements.statement: Submitting the add-product form with a name, SKU, unit cost, quantity and low-stock threshold adds a row to the product list showing exactly the entered values

requirements.source_phrase: Users can add a product with a name, SKU, unit cost, quantity and low-stock threshold
requirements.statement: POST /api/products stores every field the form sends (name, sku, unit_cost, quantity, low_stock_threshold) and GET /api/products/{id} from a new session returns those same values

requirements.source_phrase: The product list shows each product's name, SKU, on-hand quantity and stock value
requirements.statement: /products lists the workspace's products with name, SKU, quantity, unit cost and stock value per row, and the list renders an explicit empty message rather than a blank area when the workspace has no products

requirements.source_phrase: The product list shows each product's name, SKU, on-hand quantity and stock value
requirements.statement: GET /api/products returns every product of the caller's workspace with its stock value computed from the stored quantity and unit cost, and returns an empty list (not an error) for a workspace with no products

requirements.source_phrase: Users can edit a product's name, unit cost and low-stock threshold
requirements.statement: Editing a product's name, unit cost or threshold from its detail screen saves the change, the row updates in place, and a page reload still shows the new values

requirements.source_phrase: Users can edit a product's name, unit cost and low-stock threshold
requirements.statement: PATCH /api/products/{id} persists each edited field and GET /api/products/{id} from a new session returns the new values, leaving unedited fields unchanged

requirements.source_phrase: Users can delete a product they no longer stock
requirements.statement: Deleting a product asks for confirmation naming the product, removes its row from the list, and the row is still gone after a page reload

requirements.source_phrase: Users can delete a product they no longer stock
requirements.statement: DELETE /api/products/{id} removes the product and its stock movements; GET /api/products/{id} afterwards returns not-found and the product no longer appears in any listing or count

requirements.source_phrase: Staff record stock coming in and going out as movements rather than overwriting the number
requirements.statement: Recording a stock movement of +10 or -3 on a product's detail screen changes the on-hand quantity by exactly that delta and adds a line to the movement history showing the delta, the resulting quantity, the author and the time
requirements.notes: The movement is a delta, not an absolute overwrite; the history line is what proves it.

requirements.source_phrase: Staff record stock coming in and going out as movements rather than overwriting the number
requirements.statement: POST /api/products/{id}/movements with a delta stores the movement, moves the stored quantity by that delta, and GET /api/products/{id}/movements from a new session lists it with author and timestamp

requirements.source_phrase: Products below their threshold are flagged low in the list
requirements.statement: A product whose on-hand quantity is at or below its low-stock threshold shows a low-stock badge on the list and detail screens, and the badge disappears once stock is raised above the threshold

requirements.source_phrase: Products below their threshold are flagged low in the list
requirements.statement: GET /api/products?low_stock=true returns exactly the caller's workspace products whose quantity is at or below their own threshold, and excludes a product one unit above its threshold
requirements.notes: Boundary case: quantity equal to the threshold counts as low; one unit above does not.

requirements.source_phrase: The dashboard shows total inventory value and how many products are low on stock
requirements.statement: /dashboard shows the workspace's total inventory value and the count of low-stock products, and both figures change on screen after a stock movement is recorded

requirements.source_phrase: The dashboard shows total inventory value and how many products are low on stock
requirements.statement: GET /api/dashboard returns total inventory value equal to the sum over the workspace's products of quantity times unit cost, rounded to the cent, plus a low-stock count equal to the number of rows the low-stock filter returns
requirements.notes: Inputs: stored quantity and unit_cost per product; formula sum(qty*cost); units are the workspace currency's minor unit; half-up rounding to the cent.

requirements.source_phrase: Users can search products by name or SKU and filter by category
requirements.statement: Typing a word from a product name or SKU into the search box lists the matching products and no product from another workspace, and clearing the box restores the full list

requirements.source_phrase: Users can search products by name or SKU and filter by category
requirements.statement: GET /api/products?q={term} matches on name and SKU case-insensitively and returns only rows from the caller's workspace; the filter offers every category value the stored data holds, not only a hard-coded list

requirements.source_phrase: An owner can invite teammates by email into their workspace
requirements.statement: An owner can invite a teammate by email from the members screen, the invite appears as pending with the address typed, and the invited person signing in with that address joins the same workspace

requirements.source_phrase: An owner can invite teammates by email into their workspace
requirements.statement: POST /api/workspaces/{id}/invites records the invitation bound to that workspace; accepting it adds the user to that workspace only and never to another workspace with the same email domain

requirements.source_phrase: These limits must be enforced on the server, not merely hidden in the screen
requirements.statement: A Staff member sending DELETE /api/products/{id} or PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}/settings directly is refused, and the product and settings are unchanged afterwards, while an Owner performing the same request succeeds
requirements.notes: Both halves are required: the refusal for the least-privileged role and the success for the owner, so over-refusal is detectable.

requirements.source_phrase: not being able to reach another company's data even by following a direct link or guessing an identifier
requirements.statement: A signed-in member of workspace B requesting GET /api/products/{id} or GET /api/products/{id}/movements with an id from workspace A is refused and receives no field of that product or its movements
requirements.notes: Direct-link and guessed-id boundary; the response must carry no partial payload.

requirements.source_phrase: Users can export the product list to CSV
requirements.statement: Clicking export on /products downloads a CSV named for the workspace and date whose rows are the products the screen is currently showing, including their quantities and stock values

requirements.source_phrase: Users can export the product list to CSV
requirements.statement: GET /api/products/export.csv returns a well-formed CSV whose header names the exported columns and whose rows and stock-value totals equal what the filtered list returns, scoped to the caller's workspace
requirements.notes: Judged by file content, not by response status: it must open as CSV and hold the same rows the screen shows.

requirements.statement: Creating a second product with a SKU already stored in the same workspace is refused by the store and stores no second row, including when two identical submissions arrive together
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of product creation: the unique SKU is a store constraint, not a form check, and the concurrent case is the one that exposes a read-then-write race.

requirements.statement: A stock movement that would take the on-hand quantity below zero is refused, no movement row is written, and the stored quantity is unchanged
requirements.notes: Boundary value of the stock calculation; also proves the failure path writes nothing half-way.

requirements.statement: A stock movement may be dated in the past and is accepted with that date; a movement dated in the future is refused and moves no quantity
requirements.notes: A ledger entry legitimately records something that already happened; a future-dated movement would corrupt the on-hand figure.

requirements.statement: The quantity and stock value a product row displays equal the values GET /api/products returns for that product after a reload, never a value left over from a previous row or from the browser only
GET /api/products, GET /api/dashboard and GET /api/products?low_stock=true for a brand-new workspace each return an empty result with zero totals rather than an error
After signing out from the header the app returns to /signin and makes no further signed-in request; pressing back does not render the previous workspace's product data
After sign-out the previous session token is refused by GET /api/products, and the token issued for a different session still works, so sign-out revokes one session only
A workspace with a thousand products renders its list by page and the first page appears in about the time a five-product list does, with the row count stated on screen
GET /api/products over a thousand stored rows returns each matching product exactly once across its pages, and the total count equals the number of rows the pages contain
A search term, category filter and sort order applied on /products survive a page reload and back-navigation, and clearing the filters resets the list to every product

Every stock value and total the API returns equals quantity times unit cost summed for its scope and rounded to the cent, so the product row, the dashboard total and the CSV export report the same figure for the same data
requirements.notes: Business logic class: one formula, one precision, applied on the list, the dashboard and the export path alike.

requirements.statement: The stock value shown on a product row, the inventory total on /dashboard and the figure in the exported CSV are identical for the same product and no value is rounded differently in one place than another

For any product, the currently stored quantity equals the starting quantity plus the sum of the deltas in its movement history, and deleting a movement is either refused or recomputes the quantity to match
requirements.notes: The ledger and the running total must not drift; this is the invariant that catches a double-applied movement.

requirements.statement: GET / serves the application shell and every asset it references, so /products, /dashboard and /settings each load with no 404 for a script or stylesheet and no unstyled flash
requirements.notes: Shared backend for the presentation-only frontend requirements (contrast, layout, routing, no-leak, build).

requirements.statement: Body text, table headers and the low-stock badge on /products meet at least a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against their background in the app's only theme, and the low-stock badge is distinguishable without relying on colour alone
requirements.notes: Layout, theme and visuals class; the palette is served through the shell's stylesheet.

requirements.statement: /products and /dashboard show their primary content without overlap or clipping at 1440px and at 375px wide, with the add-product action start-visible rather than behind a collapsed menu
Saving a product or a stock movement shows a confirmation naming the thing saved, and a refused save shows a message in the user's terms stating what was rejected; nothing succeeds or fails silently
A refused write returns a machine-readable error naming the field or rule that failed, and the client can render it without an unhandled exception or a bare stack trace
When a save, delete or stock movement fails the screen shows a message in the user's terms saying what went wrong, and the product list still shows the pre-action values
The header, page titles and empty-state copy name the product consistently and match the product the request describes, with no placeholder text or lorem ipsum on any screen
The URL reflects the current screen, so opening /products/{id} directly or reloading it lands on that product's detail with its data, and forward and back move between the screens already visited
requirements.notes: UI state, navigation and interaction class.

requirements.statement: On /products the loading, empty, populated and error states look visibly different from one another, and a control that renders performs its action exactly once and then shows its own new state
Opening /products or /dashboard while signed out redirects to /signin rather than rendering a blank page or another workspace's data
requirements.notes: Auth, sessions and access control class.

requirements.statement: Any /api route other than signup and signin refuses a request with no session or an expired session and returns no workspace data
A session token stays valid while the user works and refreshes before it expires, so a save made after twenty minutes of work still succeeds with no re-login
